gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-moderustic: Moderustic is a modern sans whose curves look traced with a broad nib and left a little unfinished. Shantell Sans on top draws every stroke at a single thickness, and that loose, hand-drawn cable of a line is what makes this pairing memorable.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-molengo: Expressive and a bit cheeky, Shantell Sans draws plain constant-width lines with a mouth as wide as a tin can's lid. Molengo follows with generous gaps between its strokes, so tiny text stays crisp under the heading's playful swagger.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-momo-trust-sans: Momo Trust Sans has bowls as heavy as its stems and curved letters with wide, unclosed mouths, which makes it feel friendly and sturdy. And Shantell Sans above it feels looser and more hand-made, so the two sit together like a doodle beside a clean label.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-mona-sans: Shantell Sans draws every outline with one heavy, unvarying stroke. It gives a headline real personality, while Mona Sans keeps its letter openings wide, like a door left ajar, and simply gets on with being readable.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-monda: Shantell Sans skims along with a stroke that never changes weight, giving it a loose, easy feel. And that quality earns its keep in big, short lines, while Monda stays tidy beneath with small counters that never feel clogged.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-mooli: Mooli is a sans with open, round letters that stay clear even when the text gets very small. Shantell Sans pairs a hand-traced line of constant weight against it, adding a playful voice.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-murecho: Murecho is a plain sans with s curves that open wide at both ends, so it feels modern and tidy. And under Shantell Sans, whose line looks like a fixed-width stencil brush, a long passage would read smoothly and without fuss.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-nanum-gothic: A mouth as wide as a tin can's cut lid, drawn with one fixed nib width, gives Shantell Sans its expressive look. Nanum Gothic, a plain sans, has wide channels leading into each counter, and that quiet openness is where the pair really works.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-national-park: National Park is a sans-serif drawn as if by a pen that never changes pressure or angle, with rounded letters and a clearly open side. Shantell Sans is the one to show off with, while this body just stays out of the way.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-niramit: Niramit is a sans whose letter curves look like they are gaping, which gives it a clean, professional face. But Shantell Sans is the showier one, with no modulation between stems and connecting strokes, while Niramit is the one you read.
